topic.title: <ResponsiveGroup>
topic.p: <ResponsiveGroup/> tells its managed GuiResponsiveCompositionBase to switch view at the same time when itself is required to do so.
<ResponsiveGroup/> is a GuiResponsiveCompositionBase and a <Bounds/>.

topic.title: Managing child GuiResponsiveCompositionBase
topic.p: When things inside a <ResponsiveGroup/> are changed, <ResponsiveGroup/> will search for any child composition that is a GuiResponsiveCompositionBase. If a child composition is not, it will search into this child composition and see if there are any GuiResponsiveCompositionBase recursively. When a GuiResponsiveCompositionBase is found, it stops searching for child compositions inside this GuiResponsiveCompositionBase.
Eventually <ResponsiveGroup/> knows all child GuiResponsiveCompositionBase inside it.
IMPORTANT: If a child GuiResponsiveCompositionBase shares no axis with the group's Direction, it is not a managed GuiResponsiveCompositionBase.

topic.title: <ResponsiveGroup>::Direction
topic.p: The default value for this property is Both.
Valid values for this property are Horizontal, Vertical and Both.
When Direction is Horizontal, it only reacts to changing to its width. When Direction is Vertical, it only reacts to changing to its height.

topic.title: <ResponsiveGroup>::LevelCount
topic.p: This property represents how many different views the group can have. It is the largest of 1, the number of ViewSizes entries, and the LevelCount of every managed GuiResponsiveCompositionBase.
ViewSizes contributes permanent levels even without managed children. With an empty array and no managed children, LevelCount is 1.

topic.title: <ResponsiveGroup>::CurrentLevel
topic.p: This property represents the current view of a <ResponsiveGroup/>.
The smallest view is 0, the largest view is LevelCount - 1. The group takes the largest current level among its permanent ViewSizes contribution and its managed children.

topic.title: <ResponsiveGroup>::ViewSizes
topic.p: ViewSizes is an optional integer array of preferred minimum sizes indexed by CurrentLevel. Write entries from small to large: entry 0 belongs to level 0. This order is the reverse of the largest-first Views collection of <ResponsiveView/>.

An array with N entries contributes N permanent levels. Assigning it initializes its own current level to N - 1, like a newly configured <ResponsiveView/>. These levels and their current state remain available when all responsive children are removed. Children can contribute additional levels; children with fewer levels stay at their largest view.

For an array with N entries and current level L, use ViewSizes[L] when L < N. Otherwise use ViewSizes[N - 1] + (L - N + 1). For example, {64 230} contributes levels 0 and 1 with sizes 64 and 230. If a child contributes level 2, its preferred size is 231.

Horizontal applies the selected value to PreferredMinSize.x and preserves its height. Vertical applies it to PreferredMinSize.y and preserves its width. Both applies the same value to both components. The group reapplies the value on assignment, level or direction changes, and minimum-size measurement. Manually setting an affected component of PreferredMinSize does not override ViewSizes.

Both literal XML forms below are supported without an eval binder. Child content is omitted here. In C++, SetViewSizes(const collections::Array<vint>&) copies the array; GetViewSizes() returns a const reference containing only the configured entries, without extrapolated values. Reflection exposes an assignable typed integer-array property.
<ResponsiveGroup Direction="Horizontal" ViewSizes="{64 230}"> <!-- Account rows --> </ResponsiveGroup>
<ResponsiveGroup Direction="Horizontal"> <att.ViewSizes><_>120</_><_>334</_></att.ViewSizes> <!-- Movie rows --> </ResponsiveGroup>

With virtualized lists, initialize newly realized responsive rows to their group's established level before attaching them. With ViewSizes supplying the row appearances, removing all rows preserves the configured levels and the group's own current level. Replacement rows can use group.CurrentLevel directly, without separate application fields or restoration handlers. Keep the movie group's original CurrentLevelChanged handler calling ReloadVisibleStyles() to reset the arranger's row height when switching between compact and detailed templates. Only configured levels are permanent; levels contributed solely by removed children disappear.
The standalone Responsive3 tutorial demonstrates both ViewSizes forms, row initialization before attachment, and row-height refreshes.

topic.title: Choosing a view
topic.p: When a <ResponsiveGroup/> is required to switch to a larger view (increasing CurrentLevel by 1), or when a <ResponsiveGroup/> is required to switch to a smaller view (decreasing CurrentLevel by 1), it tells all managed GuiResponsiveCompositionBase to synchronize with that new CurrentLevel. If any GuiResponsiveCompositionBase's LevelCount is not large enough, it stays with its largest view.
